subject.title: [Feature] Queue prompts when API limits prevent an immediate response

question: Should OpenClaw core own a durable provider-capacity prompt queue, and should the open followup-persistence and provider-cooldown PRs be folded into that design?
rationale: The issue is not a narrow broken line fix: it defines a storage and UX contract across provider limits, session recovery, queue visibility, and replay guarantees.

options.title: Sponsor Core Queue Design
options.body: Keep this issue as the canonical tracker and require a SQLite-backed design that coordinates provider cooldown state, visible waiting status, and exactly-once replay.

options.title: Narrow Existing PRs
options.body: Let the open followup and provider PRs solve their smaller restart/cooldown slices while leaving provider-capacity prompt queuing for a later explicit design.

options.title: Decline Core Queueing
options.body: Close this direction as out of scope and require clients, providers, or plugins to manage capacity waiting outside OpenClaw orchestration.

recommendation.title: Sponsor Core Queue Design
recommendation.body: Keep this issue as the canonical tracker and require a SQLite-backed design that coordinates provider cooldown state, visible waiting status, and exactly-once replay.

likelyOwner.reason: The queue-mode and followup lifecycle history makes steipete the best available owner for deciding whether this becomes a core queue contract.
